findings.finding: The arch head reads as a flattened, nearly square dark lintel at 1x, not a pointed Gothic arch, so it matches the lancet windows of the chipset less well.
findings.fix: Step the inner dark opening in by 1px per row over the top 3 rows toward a 2px apex, and add a 1px light keystone pixel at the apex in the stone frame.

findings.finding: The lower treads on the floor row, with brass rods over the red runner, read slightly as ladder rungs because the tread and riser bands are similar in height.
findings.fix: Make the bottom-row tread tops 2px light and the risers 1px dark, and let the runner fold darker on each riser so each step reads as a plane plus a face.

findings.finding: At 1x the light 2px rim on north/west/east plus the dark north inner wall can momentarily read as a standing frame or fireplace opening rather than a hole cut into the floor. The side rails end with slightly brighter south tips that hint at posts.
findings.fix: Darken the south 1px of each side rail to the rim-shadow tone so the rails end flush with the floor. Drop the north rim highlight to mid-stone so only the inner (top-left lit) edges carry the light tone.

findings.finding: The bottom-row oak steps are tall, flat orange blocks with weak tread/riser separation, so they read more like crates than steps when seen beside the student sprite.
findings.fix: Give each lower step a 2px lighter oak top and a 1px dark-brown riser shadow line, and shrink the visible riser height toward the top.

findings.finding: The light stone arch frame almost disappears at 1x between the two bookcases: the oak steps dominate, so the doorway reads as one more brown cabinet bay.
findings.fix: Add a 1px dark outline outside the stone jambs and brighten the jamb highlight on the west side by one palette step so the stone separates from the oak shelves.

findings.finding: The grey stone treads have low tread/riser contrast in the lower half, and the straw and dropping specks read as noise at 1x.
findings.fix: Raise the front-edge highlight to the lightest stone tone on every tread, deepen the risers by one step, and keep at most two 1px straw specks plus the single dropping.

findings.finding: The white feather on the nearest tread is a 2-3px white blob at 1x and reads as a stray pixel or paper scrap.
findings.fix: Draw the feather as a 3px diagonal with a 1px light-grey shaft shadow, oriented top-left to bottom-right.

findings.finding: This piece has the same 1x frame-vs-hole ambiguity as the castle down stairwell, and the wooden rim is a bit heavy.
findings.fix: Use the same fix as the castle down stairwell: flatten the south tips of the side rails and darken the north rim highlight.

places.finding: Clocktower: the riveted iron frame sits right against the round gear porthole on the north wall, so the wall face looks crowded and the frame's east post nearly touches the porthole rim.
places.fix: Shift the gear porthole 1 tile east, or leave a clear 1-tile stone wall gap between the frame and the porthole.

places.finding: Honeydukes: a candy-box stack sits directly south of the stair entrance cell, so the walk-in path is approached from the side. This is unchanged from BEFORE.
places.fix: Move the box stack one tile south-east so the cell south of the entrance is free floor.

places.finding: Owlery: the stairwell sits flush against the west wall pillar, and the light wooden west rail merges with the pale stone wall edge at 1x.
places.fix: Darken the outer 1px of the west rail, or place the stairwell one tile east.
